purpose: Fix the NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE violation where the orchestrator's own instrument-level fault isolation (a genuine, correct design - see orchestrator.ts's own header comment) could let an AnalysisRun complete as COMPLETED/COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW while an instrument's real unexpected failure existed only in an in-memory array (instrumentErrors) and, at most, a console-adjacent summary folded into fatalError text for the total-failure case only.
priorGapConfirmed: Before this fix: a per-instrument failure was caught (good fault isolation), pushed into an in-memory `instrumentErrors` array, and then - if AT LEAST ONE instrument succeeded - completely discarded: `completeAnalysisRun` had no parameter carrying this information at all, so the run would resolve to COMPLETED or COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW purely based on `openReviewItemCount`, with zero durable trace that instrument B ever failed.

newModel.name: AnalysisRunIssue
newModel.fields: id, runId (FK, cascade), companyId (FK, cascade), instrumentKey, documentIds (String[]), failedStage, errorClass, message (sanitized), createdAt.
newModel.idempotencyKey: @@unique([runId, instrumentKey]) - upserted, since the orchestrator's own per-instrument loop runs each unit at most once per attempt.
newModel.lifecycleDiscipline: Rows for a given runId are CLEARED at the start of every fresh claim of ownership of that run row (both the brand-new-row and the reclaimed-existing-row paths in startOrResumeAnalysisRun), then freshly re-populated only for instruments that actually fail during THAT attempt - mirroring lib/contract-model/compiler/persistence.ts's own established P1-9 tombstoning discipline (delete-then-repopulate within one run's own scope), applied here at run-attempt granularity rather than per-document. This prevents a resolved-on-retry instrument from leaving a stale FAILED issue row behind once it genuinely succeeds on a later attempt of the SAME AnalysisRun row (AnalysisRun rows are upserted in place across reruns, never re-minted per attempt, so without this the issue table would only ever grow).

statusModelDecision.options considered: (a) Overload COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW to also mean 'and/or an instrument failed', disambiguated only by checking AnalysisRunIssue. (b) A NEW status, PARTIAL, that takes priority whenever any instrument failed, regardless of review-item count.
statusModelDecision.rationale: The charter itself warns against overloading a status ambiguously ('the system must be able to answer did all instruments finish analysis without reconstructing from logs'). COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW answers a DIFFERENT question ('did the pipeline finish and find something a human should look at') from 'did every instrument's own analysis code path complete without throwing.' Making PARTIAL take priority over COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW when both conditions are true (some instruments failed AND some open review items exist) means AnalysisRun.status alone is a complete, unambiguous answer to the first question - a caller never needs to guess whether 'no PARTIAL status but a nonzero reviewItemCount' means 'genuinely fine, some claims need review' or 'silently missing an instrument's worth of analysis'; those are now mechanically distinguishable by status alone, with AnalysisRunIssue providing the WHAT/WHY detail behind a PARTIAL verdict.

fixDesign.neverFailsTheWholeRunForOneUnrelatedInst: The prior 'every instrument failed -> whole run FAILED' behavior is UNCHANGED and preserved exactly (this remains the one genuinely fatal whole-run case, since there is nothing meaningful to report as a partial success) - PARTIAL is reached only when instrumentOutcomes.length > 0 AND instrumentErrors.length > 0, i.e. at least one instrument's real, successfully-computed trusted state exists alongside at least one real failure. That successful instrument's own state (structural persistence, package-graph, ClaimReviewItem, and now SemanticTruthRecord - AUDIT-F1) is never discarded or rolled back because a sibling instrument failed.

everyFailureDurablyRecordedIncludingTota: Unlike the prior implementation (which folded only the FIRST instrument's error message into fatalError's own summary text for the total-failure case, silently discarding the rest), this fix records an AnalysisRunIssue row for EVERY instrument in `instrumentErrors`, unconditionally, before deciding whether the overall run is FAILED (all failed) or PARTIAL (some succeeded) - an audit reading AnalysisRunIssue sees every real failure either way.
retrySemanticsDefined: Because AnalysisRun rows are upserted in place per (companyId, packageKey, analysisAlgorithmVersion) identity (never re-minted per attempt) and this workstream's own AUDIT-F2 fix allows any non-RUNNING status (including PARTIAL and FAILED) to be safely reclaimed and rerun immediately, simply re-triggering runContractAnalysis for the SAME document set causes ALL instruments - including the one that previously failed - to be reprocessed. The previously-succeeding instrument's own reprocessing is a real, cheap, idempotent no-op at the persistence layer (SemanticTruthRecord's own contentHash-gated version-bump logic, ClaimReviewItem's own dedup-by-claimKey logic), so retrying the WHOLE run to fix ONE failed instrument is safe by construction, not merely assumed safe. A future, smaller refinement (retrying ONLY the failed instrument's own document subset, skipping already-succeeded ones outright) is a legitimate optimization this design does not preclude, but is not required to close this finding, since the full-run retry is already safe and correct.

injectionMethodDisclosure.finding: Every REAL analytical stage in this pipeline (discovery/compilation/verification) already has its OWN internal per-section/per-candidate fault isolation, confirmed empirically while building this fix's own test: a thrown discoveryCaller exception is caught internally by runDiscoveryPipeline's own per-section try/catch and degrades to a reduced/empty discovery result, never propagating to this orchestrator's own per-instrument boundary at all.
injectionMethodDisclosure.implication: This is a GOOD, correct property of those modules (not a gap this fix needs to touch), but it means the test proving AUDIT-F3's fix could not realistically inject a failure via an LLM-caller throw (as an earlier draft attempted) - see 14-partial-instrument-failure-results.json for the actual, legitimate injection method used (vi.mock on this workstream's OWN new persistSemanticTruthForInstrument, which has no internal per-object fault isolation by design, since a real failure while persisting durable semantic-truth state IS a genuine instrument-level failure, not a per-claim one).
